unit: Unit 13: Making Your Computer Easier to Use
title: Spoken descriptions
drDigitalIntro:
A screen reader says out loud whatever you are pointing at.
• It is what people who cannot see the screen use to operate a computer entirely by ear.
• It also helps anyone who finds reading tiring, or who wants confirmation before they click something.
• On this practice computer the words appear in a black bar along the bottom instead of being spoken, so you can see exactly what a real screen reader would say.
• Turn it on, then move your mouse over the dock and watch the bar change.

steps.say: Click Accessibility in the list on the left.
Click the switch next to Spoken Descriptions, then hover over the dock.

drDigitalSuccess: Move your mouse across the dock — the bar at the bottom names each app as you reach it.
drDigitalHint: Spoken Descriptions is the last switch on the Accessibility page.
